title: Polyphosphate modulates the stress-responsive formation of functional RNA-protein condensates in bacteria and mammalian cells
experiments_summary: The study employed a broad array of in vivo, in vitro, and biochemical methods. In E. coli, chromosomal hfq was replaced with hfq-mCherry or hfq-PAmCherry in wild-type (WT) and Δppk (polyphosphate kinase deletion) strains, as well as Δppx, ΔtmaR, Δhfq, and combined deletion backgrounds. Cells were subjected to nitrogen (N) starvation (using defined Gutnick minimal media with limiting NH4Cl) or osmotic stress (1.17 M NaCl in LB) to induce polyP accumulation and Hfq foci formation. A plasmid-encoded hyperactive polyphosphate kinase variant (Ppk10k) was expressed in the Δppk strain to artificially elevate polyP. PolyP was extracted and visualized on TBE gels using chain-length markers, and quantified colorimetrically after enzymatic degradation with yeast exopolyphosphatase (yPpx). ATP levels were measured using a bioluminescence assay. Hfq foci number, size, and intensity were quantified by fluorescence microscopy with automated image segmentation (Omnipose), and foci were dissolved with 1,6-hexanediol to assess liquid-like properties. Immunofluorescence on fixed bacteria used an anti-FLAG antibody (for 3×FLAG-Hfq) and a GFP-fused polyP-binding domain probe (PPXPD-GFP) to co-stain Hfq and polyP. Single-molecule super-resolution microscopy (PALM/SMLM) with Hfq-PAmCherry was used to measure diffusion coefficients and classify Hfq into condensate (C-state), nucleoid-bound (B-state), and free (F-state) subpopulations using the SMALL-LABS tracking algorithm and three-state cumulative distribution function fitting. FRAP measurements on similarly sized Hfq foci in WT and Δppk strains assessed condensate fluidity. Protein solubility fractionation by differential centrifugation and SDS-PAGE quantified insoluble versus soluble Hfq fractions. N-starvation survival and recovery upon N-replenishment were measured as colony-forming units (CFUs) and OD600, respectively, in WT, Δppk, Δhfq, and Δppk/Δhfq strains, with plasmid-borne ppk or hfq rescue controls. Co-localization of RNase E-mTurquoise2, Enolase-mTurquoise2, and RhlB-mTurquoise2 with Hfq-mCherry foci was assessed by dual-color fluorescence microscopy in WT and Δppk strains. Native PAGE (4–20% TBE gels, 100 V, 16 h) followed by western blotting was used to examine high-molecular-weight (HMW) Hfq-mCherry assemblies in N-0 and N-24 lysates treated with DNase I, RNase A, or yPpx. For proteomic characterization, gel bands corresponding to HMW Hfq complexes were excised from native PAGE gels of WT, Δppk, and yPpx-treated WT lysates; proteins were in-gel trypsin-digested, dimethyl-labeled, and analyzed by LC-MS/MS on an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos. Anti-mCherry co-immunoprecipitation (RFP-Trap magnetic agarose beads) from N-0 and N-24 WT and Δppk lysates was performed, and co-precipitated proteins were identified by LC-MS/MS. GO term enrichment analysis was conducted using iPAGE on the MS-identified HMW Hfq-associated proteins. For RNA analyses, fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) with an AF647-labeled poly(A) probe was performed on fixed N-24 WT and Δppk bacteria. Poly(A) tail length distributions were measured genome-wide using a custom RNA-seq library preparation (3′-adapter ligation, reverse transcription, second-strand synthesis, sequencing on NextSeq 1000) followed by computational quantification of terminal adenosine runs. Transcript stability was determined by transcriptional shutdown assays using rifampicin treatment of N-24 WT and Δppk cells, with ERCC spike-in normalization and exponential decay modeling of RNA-seq time-course data (0, 10, 30, 60 min) generated on a NextSeq 2000. In vitro, purified Hfq (with 4% Cy3-HfqS65C) was combined with AF647-polyP-300 and/or FAM-rA30 RNA in HEPES buffer, and phase separation was imaged by confocal microscopy in pluronic acid-treated CultureWell slides; droplets were quantified with an automated image analysis pipeline. A phase diagram was generated by varying polyP and Hfq concentrations. Electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSA) on TBE native gels assessed ternary complex formation among Hfq, rA30 RNA, and polyP-300. In mammalian cells, NIH3T3 and HEK293 cell lines were treated with 0.5 mM sodium arsenite to induce stress granules (SGs) and P-bodies. Cells were immunostained with antibodies against the P-body marker EDC4 or DCP1A and the SG marker G3BP1, together with a PPXBD-mCherry probe to visualize polyP. A stable NIH3T3 cell line expressing an inducible destabilization domain-fused yPpx (via lentiviral transduction) was used to deplete cellular polyP; NIH3T3 cells transiently transfected with E. coli Ppk were used to elevate polyP. P-body and SG counts per cell were quantified by confocal microscopy under these conditions. GO term overlaps between the H-body proteome and human P-body/SG proteomes (from the RNA granule database) were assessed by permutation testing.
